as_of_note: Compiled 2026-10-30 by the Saudi Arabia source-audit lane. CONTEXT ONLY: never a scoring input. Every value was read from the cited document in this session; mixed vintages (2022-2025) are stated per row and must not be combined into one 'current' picture. Bases differ by source (country totals from EIA; company totals from Aramco; grid-connected capacity from SEC) and are labelled on each row. OPEC, Energy Institute and Saudi government sites were not machine-readable on this date, so no figure is taken from them. See docs/countries/SA_SOURCE_AUDIT.md.

metrics.basis: country total; 85% petroleum liquids, 15% natural gas, 0% coal
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia, Table 1 (last updated 2024-10-04)

metrics.basis: country total, crude oil only (EIA International Energy Statistics)
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia (last updated 2024-10-04)

metrics.basis: Aramco company total; crude oil + NGL + condensate, so NOT comparable with crude_oil_production
metrics.source: Saudi Aramco, Fourth quarter and full-year 2025 results press release

metrics.basis: country total, dry gas; EIA states 4.3 Tcf in both 2022 and 2023
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia (last updated 2024-10-04)

metrics.basis: country total, EIA estimate (62% natural gas, 38% oil, <1% renewables)
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia (last updated 2024-10-04)

metrics.basis: Kingdom grid-connected capacity at end of Q3 2025 (SEC 55,962; IPP & IWPP 22,572; Others 15,324). Excludes most captive generation: Aramco reports 6.3 GW captive in 2025, of which 0.5 GW was supplied to the grid
metrics.source: Saudi Electricity Company, Earnings Release Q3 2025 (November 2025)

metrics.basis: GROSS (100% physical) capacity of the nine in-Kingdom refineries in which Aramco holds an interest, as at 2025-12-31: the sum of the per-refinery figures in Aramco's 2025 Annual Report. Per-facility figures are deliberately not reproduced here. Completeness against non-Aramco refineries not yet researched
metrics.source: Saudi Aramco, Annual Report 2025, Results and performance section (Downstream, refinery footprint)

metrics.basis: NET (Aramco equity share) of the same nine refineries, computed from the published gross capacities and Aramco's published effective ownership. A financial basis: do NOT use as an exposure denominator
metrics.source: Saudi Aramco, Annual Report 2025, Results and performance section (Downstream)

metrics.basis: Aramco (the Company) total crude oil exports, company basis
metrics.source: Saudi Aramco, Annual Report 2025, Results and performance section (Supply and trading)

metrics.basis: country total per EIA (down from 7.4 million b/d in 2022); different basis and year from the Aramco company figure
metrics.source: U.S. EIA, Country Analysis Brief: Saudi Arabia (last updated 2024-10-04)

significance: Crude oil and other petroleum liquids made up 85% of Saudi Arabia's primary energy production in 2022 and natural gas 15%, with no coal production (EIA).
Saudi Arabia meets all of its natural gas consumption with domestic production (EIA, 2024).
In 2023 an estimated 62% of Saudi electricity was generated from natural gas and 38% from oil, with renewables under 1% (EIA).

Aramco reports five wholly-owned and four affiliated refineries in the Kingdom, which together accounted for 63% of its 4.2 million b/d net refining capacity at the end of 2025 (Aramco Annual Report 2025).
